import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_4.csv"
]

# Read all source CSV files into dataframes with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files[0], index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files[1], index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files[2], index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files[3], index_col=0)
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_files[4], index_col=0)

# All source tables have the exact same schema: ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
# According to Hint 2 and Hint 4, since schemas are identical and match the target schema,
# we can simply UNION (concatenate) all source tables.

# Concatenate all source dataframes vertically (union)
df_all = pd.concat([df0, df1, df2, df3, df4], ignore_index=True)

# The target schema is:
# ['Year': string, 'Category': string, 'Nominee': string, 'Movie': string, 'Winner': string]
# Ensure all columns are strings (object dtype in pandas)
for col in ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']:
    df_all[col] = df_all[col].astype(str)

# The target examples show that the 'Winner' column contains "YES" or presumably "NO" or other values.
# We keep it as is.

# No aggregation or group by is needed because the target examples have no indication of aggregation,
# and the source tables have the same schema and can be unioned directly.

# Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV file path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_all.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
